article.title: Common mistake: 'from' vs 'since' for time
article.description: Wrong: 'I have lived here from 2015.' Right: 'I have lived here since 2015.' Teaching point: use 'since' with present perfect for a starting point still relevant now; 'from' is used with a defined start AND end point, like 'The offer is valid from Monday to Friday.'
article.content: Wrong: 'I have lived here from 2015.' Right: 'I have lived here since 2015.' Teaching point: use 'since' with present perfect for a starting point still relevant now; 'from' is used with a defined start AND end point, like 'The offer is valid from Monday to Friday.'

generated.caption:
Ever said 'I have lived here from 2015' and felt a bit off? 🤔 Here's why!

Use 'since' with the present perfect for a starting point that's still true now. For example: 'I have lived here since 2015.' 'From' needs a clear start AND end point, like 'The offer is valid from Monday to Friday.'

Got it? Save this tip and follow for daily lessons!
generated.script: English mein 'from' aur 'since' use karne mein confuse hote ho na? Dekho, 'since' hum tab use karte hain jab koi action past mein start hua ho aur abhi bhi chal raha ho. Jaise: 'I have lived here since 2015.' Matlab 2015 se main yahan reh raha hoon aur abhi bhi yahin hoon. Lekin 'from' hum tab use karte hain jab humein start aur end dono points clear pata hon. Example: 'The offer is valid from Monday to Friday.' Yahan start aur end dono clearly defined hain. Toh simple hai: koi cheez agar past se ab tak continue ho rahi hai, toh 'since'. Agar start aur end time fixed hain, toh 'from'. Ab samajh aaya? Kaisa laga ye tip? Comment mein batao aur The English Vault ko follow karo aise hi useful tips ke liye!

slides.body: Many English learners often say, 'I have lived here from 2015.' However, this usage is incorrect. When describing an action that began in the past and continues up to the present, especially with the present perfect tense, you should always use 'since' to indicate the starting point. For example, the correct sentence is 'I have lived here since 2015.' On the other hand, 'from' is correctly used when specifying both a clear start and an end point for an event, such as in 'The offer is valid from Monday to Friday.'
